title: Optimality of the Logarithmic Gap in Erdős #728 Factorial Divisibility

problemStatement.formal: \exists\, \varepsilon > 0 : \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log n} \max\{ a + b - n : \varepsilon n \le a,b \le (1-\varepsilon)n,\ a!\,b! \mid n!\,(a+b-n)! \} = +\infty ?
problemStatement.plain: Erdős proved that when a!·b! divides n!·(a+b-n)! (with a,b a bounded fraction of n), the sum a+b exceeds n by at most O(log n). The parent proof shows this logarithmic gap is achievable infinitely often. This companion problem asks whether log n is the true ceiling: can we prove that no admissible triple ever achieves a super-logarithmic gap, confirming the gap is exactly Θ(log n) and cannot be improved beyond O(log n)?
whyMatters: Completes the two-sided asymptotic characterization g(n) = Θ(log n), matching the parent's lower bound with Erdős's classical upper bound.
Verifies a classical Erdős result (a+b ≤ n + O(log n)) that the parent states informally but does not itself formalize.
Certifies the optimality of the AI-generated #728 construction.
